summary: Move-in: narrator parks last box, is shown around by Mrs. Hollis on the landing; Mrs. Hollis explains house rules and mentions the hall clock stopped at 4:22. Mrs. Hollis gives narrator a key.

Discovery of a silver locket hidden behind the wallpaper lining in the right-hand corner behind the wardrobe. The locket is dented; the chain is nearly absent; a red-brown smear runs along the rim (appears like rust or dried mud). Inside is a faded sepia photograph of a child with a broken toy; the reverse is scratched with initials 'E.L.' The piece smells faintly of old soap and a hint of lavender; a scatter of powder dusts the hinge. The metal's wear suggests early twentieth-century manufacture or long wear; chain condition does not match metal wear. The narrator pockets the locket and records it in a notebook.

Two instances of measured footsteps above the narrator's room recorded in the notebook: "2:00 a.m. — footsteps above." and "3:12 a.m. — footsteps above." The narrator notes a patterned cadence (pair of thuds, pause, another pair).
Narrator climbed the narrow ladder and accessed the attic at 9:14 a.m.; attic lit by cold gable light and smelled of dust and old varnish.
Found damp chalk smudges in a crescent on the trapdoor hinge; the chalk was soft to the touch. A jar nearby bore pale handprints in chalk powder, the powder feeling faintly tacky when brushed.

Found a porcelain doll beneath the dented lid of a tea tin on the central joist at 9:21 a.m.; doll missing one glass eye, braided ribbon knotted to its wrist, dried mud on the hem, smelled of dust and garden earth.

Found a cloth-covered diary wedged under a beam along the northern eaves at 9:26 a.m.; contains short dated entries in a child's hand and a drawing of a toy with a bent wheel; a page had been torn out and its torn corner folded into the lining.

Levered up a loose plank three boards from the trapdoor at 9:33 a.m., revealing a narrow bundle of papers and envelopes the size of a child's palm; beneath them the subfloor had a dark, dry stain that smelled faintly of iron and old cloth.
Observed an unexplained smear along the rim of the silver locket (a dark/red-brown mark) while comparing the locket photograph to the diary drawing.
Noted that the attic's joists and hollow cavities transmit footfalls into the bedroom below, producing a precise resonance that could translate attic wood into a felt sensation under a pillow.
Placed phone on mantel, started recorder facing the stairs; recorder created file 2026-03-03_11-11-00_mantel_record.wav.
Photographed the stopped clock; the hands sat at 4:22 and the stop did not appear theatrical. Photo saved as 2026-03-03_clock_4-22_front.jpg.
Propped sepia photograph against cracked mirror and used raking light to reveal faint ink on the back reading 'Oct 12 1913'. Photo saved as 2026-03-03_sepia_back_rakinglight.jpg.

Photographed the silver locket beside the diary page and took close-ups; letters on the locket appeared to read 'E.L.' and the narrator compared the capital E in the diary photograph with the E on the locket.

Returned to the attic with a ruler and north marker, inspected and photographed the dark patch beneath the loose plank; stain appeared bruise-brown with speckled edges and a dry skin. Macro saved as 2026-03-03_stain_under_plank_macro.jpg.

Read the torn diary fragment aloud: "—spilt tea under the boards. Don't tell." Also mapped the fragment into the page context: "Oct 12 — tea and the clock. The clock stopped at four and twenty-two when Mam went for sugar."

Before climbing down, the house made two small thuds, pause, then two more; the recorder later showed distinct ticks at two predictable hours that night — the attic motion matched that small repertoire.

At the kitchen sink the narrator presented the photographs and diary fragment and read the sepia back date aloud and the locket inscription and fragment; Mrs. Hollis folded her hands tighter, slid a jar to the side, and said, 'Children left long ago,' offering no explanation and not denying the paper.
Wrote new observations into the notebook, noting sepia 'Oct 12 1913', locket inscription appearing 'E.L.', and copied the torn fragment exactly as: '—spilt tea under the boards. Don't tell.'
Narrator reads torn diary page aloud: "—spilt tea under the boards. Don't tell.".
Beneath the bundle of child's papers, narrator finds a dark, circular tannin-brown stain on the subfloor and scrapes tacky residue away, matching the diary's reference to spilt tea under the boards.
Narrator inspects silver locket and confirms initials E.L.; locket dent and letters observed under lamp.
Narrator reads/deciphers date on back of sepia photograph: October 12, 1913; date aligns with locket and diary material.

When narrator places the porcelain doll on a joist it slides into narrator's palm as if nudged by a small hand; a ribbon braided at its wrist matches the diary's instruction to fasten a ribbon so the doll would remember.
A fresh chalk letter 'E' appears on the attic hatch in a child's wobbly hand, accompanied by a child's whispered repetition: 'Don't tell.'
Mrs. Hollis confesses to concealing Elsie's accident, sealing the space and telling people the child had been sent away.
The house's small, clockwork sounds — measured footfalls and two-thud cadence — stop entirely after the evidence is presented and confession obtained.
